_comment: Reviewed person names for redaction. Candidates come from tools/find_names.py; a human decides what lands here. Roles: COACH for Trader Foundation coaches, MEMBER for students and anyone else named. Vlad is never redacted, per CLAUDE.md, because he authors the material and redacting him breaks every citation.
_reviewed_over: transcripts/raw/fb-live, 393 sessions. Original 53-name list reviewed over 23 sessions (batches 01 and 151-159 plus 0470); expanded to 192 names after the Q&A extraction pass read all 393 sessions in full and flagged names left unredacted, cross-checked against tools/find_names.py run over the full set. A handful of ambiguous candidates were deliberately left out: bare initials, ordinary words, real public figures, fragments, and confirmed word collisions found by sampling raw context per candidate (Cam = candle abbreviation, Lee = garbled 'Li Auto' ticker, Ben = garbled 'hellbent', Lulu = LULU ticker). Some kept names carry a smaller, one-off collision risk noted only here rather than fixed with a guard: Rob/rob-the-verb, Nick/nickel-jargon ('fast nick'), Scott/Scotts-Miracle-Gro.

_rejected._comment: Candidates reviewed and judged not to be people. Kept so the same words are not re-litigated on the next batch.
_rejected._note: Reviewed and confirmed not people. Opex is options expiration, Cola and Xbox are brands, the rest are ordinary words the mid-sentence rule picks up. Folded back into find_names.py so the same noise is not reported every pass.

_procedure: Redact, then run find_names.py over transcripts/clean/. Anything it still reports is a name the list did not know. Add it, re-run redact.py --force, and repeat until the clean scan is quiet. That loop is how the list grows across 555 sessions.
